paper_metadata.title: Laves phase strengthening in ultrafine-grained Co–Cr–Ta micropillars under uniaxial compression at modest temperature

evidence.quote: Here, we designed and fabricated an ultrafine-grained Co-28Cr-3Ta alloy which could retain over 80% of its room temperature yield strength at 300 ˚C, two times that of its equivalent without addition of Ta.
To illustrate the enhancement of the Laves phases, a Co-30Cr alloy of similar grain size but in the absence of Laves phases was also fabricated as control.

The bulk UFG Co-28Cr-3Ta alloy was fabricated by a combination of mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering (SPS).

To illustrate the enhancement of the Laves phases, a Co-30Cr alloy of similar grain size but in the absence of Laves phases was also fabricated as control.

Commercially pure Co (Alfa Aesar, 1.6 µm, 99.8%), Cr (Alfa Aesar, ＜10 µm, 99.5%) and Ta (Alfa Aesar, 325 mesh, 99.9%) powders were mixed with the nominal composition and subjected to high energy ball milling using a SPEX 8000D mixer in an argon glove box for 12 h at RT (25˚C).

The milled powders were subsequently packed into a graphite die with an inner diameter of 10 mm and spark plasma sintered (SPS-211Lx, Fujidempa Kogyo. Co., ltd) at 900 ˚C under 40 MPa for 5 min in vacuum.

attributes.morphology: bright contrast precipitates of relatively larger size

evidence.quote: One in bright contrast and of relatively larger size was identified to be Co-rich (Co, Cr)2Ta (defined as Co2Ta) by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDX; Fig. S1) and HRTEM (Fig. 3a).

Statistical measurements show that the average precipitate sizes of Co2Ta and Cr2Ta Laves phases are of 86 nm and 14 nm, respectively. In addition, the volume fractions of Co2Ta and Cr2Ta were determined to be 6.0% and 12.6%, respectively.

In this work, the GB strengthening increments are calculated to be 771 and 723 MPa for Co-28Cr-3Ta and Co-30Cr, respectively.
Using above parameters, the dislocation strengthening increments are calculated to be 55 and 51 MPa for Co-28Cr-3Ta and Co-30Cr, respectively.
Thus, the strength increments from solid solution are similar.
In the Co-28Cr-3Ta alloy, the precipitates of Laves phase is incoherent with the matrix, thus the Orowan mechanism is predominant.
Therefore, the operative mechanism for precipitate strengthening is Orowan dislocation bypass in the Co-30Cr alloy.
it is reasonable to hypothesize that the precipitate strengthening mechanism changes from Orowan dislocation bypass to dislocation shearing in the Co-30Cr alloy.
At modest temperature, cross-slip and climb of dislocations become easy and the GBs become weak, leading to softening of the alloys.
With increasing strain of the pillar, denser dislocation networks forms. The newly formed dislocation networks could effectively prevent the dislocation gliding and thus strengthen the alloy.
Thus, the combination of pinning effect and dual phase microstructure makes the suppression of grain growth in the Co-28Cr-3Ta alloy more evident.
